adversarialReview.check: Falsifier 3 -- the class-5 smooth-path check must be machine-executed, not planner memory.
adversarialReview.result: Design in progress, grounded in ENFORCEMENT's own stated preference ('where a type can express the constraint, prefer the type over any check') and in a live instance already found: LayerAbsenceVerdict lacked a 'refused' member the 2026-09-01 ruling required, which a discriminated-union exhaustiveness check (a switch/discriminant with no default branch, so the compiler fails when a new required state is not added to every consumer) would have caught at merge time, not at CI-skip time (the actual divergence test for this class skipped in CI because no LDT checkout was present -- itself an instance of class 9, a control that cannot fire). The deliverable-3 check will be specified as: (1) what executes -- a CI step that type-checks every enum/union declared in a ruling's frontmatter against its consumers; (2) trigger -- any commit touching a file under _decisions/ with a 'requires_implementation' field, or any change to a type file it references; (3) fails -- a non-exhaustive switch/discriminated union, or a decision file whose named function/type does not exist; (4) bypass -- named explicitly (a decision filed with no frontmatter tag bypasses it entirely, which is itself flagged as a residual gap in deliverable 3).
